finding: Cursor, Claude Code project config, Qoder, philschmid/mcp-cli, and mcpc consumption use a top-level mcpServers map.
VS Code mcp.json uses a top-level servers map rather than mcpServers.
Codex uses TOML tables named mcp_servers.<id>.
OpenCode v2 nests local and remote server entries under mcp.servers.
Global user configuration is ~/.cursor/mcp.json; project configuration is .cursor/mcp.json.
A Cursor stdio mcpServers entry requires type set to stdio and a command; args are optional.
User-scope servers are stored in ~/.claude.json; project scope uses .mcp.json.
User configuration is ~/.codex/config.toml; project overrides are .codex/config.toml for trusted projects.
The user configuration belongs to the active VS Code user profile; the supported workspace file is .vscode/mcp.json.
User-scope MCP entries live under mcpServers in ~/.qoder/settings.json.
MCP uses the mcpServers JSON shape. The required output path ~/.qoder/mcp.json is a user-confirmed project constraint; public IDE docs do not state that path.
OpenCode v2 loads one global configuration from ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json or opencode.jsonc; if both exist, MCM must require an explicit path rather than guess precedence.
mcpc consumes an explicit standard JSON config file or auto-discovers known config files; its own persistent files are sessions and OAuth profiles.
mcp-cli searches mcp_servers.json in the current directory, ~/.mcp_servers.json, then ~/.config/mcp/mcp_servers.json.
MCM v1 accepts only local stdio and Streamable HTTP. Legacy HTTP+SSE is deprecated by MCP and WebSocket is outside the user-confirmed scope.
